correctness.rationale: For each leaf i the only nontrivial comparable pair is a_i<t. Downward confluence requires each element of the top leaf set L in every leaf row, and nonemptiness when t is in the top row. Forward confluence either forces each leaf row to be contained in L (if t is absent from the top row), or is automatic using witness t. These necessary and sufficient conditions produce disjoint strata. Independent row choices and binomial identities yield C_m and H_m for all integers m>=1. Binomial Taylor bounds give both large-m ratios. A separate literal exhaustive relation enumeration checked every binary relation for m=1,2,3, including all top-row strata, and closed forms were compared to independent finite sums through m=30. The finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite formulas.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 Nelson-modal source and 2024 local intuitionistic-modal paper supply the order/accessibility confluence axioms but do not classify or enumerate their realizations on a coalescing fan. The closest public exact chain census proves a different result under totality and does not imply the non-chain fan strata, reflexive census, or distributional limits. Material-read comparisons and the completed search record reveal no stronger result that subsumes the one-top antichain cone theorem. This is best-knowledge originality, with a genuine residual priority risk from differently named ordered multirelations.

value.rationale: Coalescing fans are the first naturally branching upper-cone intuitionistic frames, so restricting the general two-confluence modal axioms to them tests non-chain behavior not captured by chain censuses. The normal form classifies all finite relation expansions for every fan width, separates T/reflexive frames exactly, and yields a genuine typical-frame phenomenon (almost sure singleton top row and exponentially rare reflexivity). These are natural structural and population invariants of a motivated logical frame class rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; the answer does not assert a broader modal completeness theorem.
